rows.name: Uber
rows.basis: Normalized non-GAAP; remove investment revaluations and unusual tax items
rows.evidence: Q2 gross bookings were $58.0B, trips grew 18%, normalized EPS was $0.81 and trailing free cash flow exceeded $10B. GAAP EPS of $1.17 included investment gains.
rows.thesis: The scarce asset is aggregated demand, payments, dispatch and local supply. AI can improve matching and support before autonomy is economically material. The strongest version of the thesis is that autonomous fleets need distribution; it is not that Uber must win vehicle manufacturing.
rows.bridge: CY2027 gross bookings of about $285B × 3.2% normalized net-income conversion ÷ 2.03B diluted shares ≈ $4.50 EPS. This requires roughly 23% growth over the Q2 bookings run rate and a modest conversion improvement.
rows.bearStory: Autonomous operators retain customers, insurance and driver costs rise, and delivery competition forces incentives; $2.60 EPS and a 16× multiple.
rows.baseStory: Demand and cross-platform usage grow; dispatch, advertising and operating efficiency improve earnings without requiring a mass robotaxi rollout.
rows.bullStory: Autonomous partnerships expand supply while Uber retains distribution economics; $5.60 EPS and 34× require strong booking growth and confidence in durable take rates.
catalysts: End-2026: Q3/Q4 booking growth, EPS conversion and autonomous-partner unit economics.
Mid-2027: evidence that autonomous markets add incremental profitable trips rather than subsidized volume.
End-2027: repeat usage, buybacks and normalized earnings establish whether the marketplace remains the customer interface.
rows.failure: Two quarters of bookings growth below 12% with deteriorating normalized operating margin, or demonstrable loss of customer ownership to autonomous fleets.
rows.risk: High disruption uncertainty. Premium rides are only one use case; this is not a pure luxury-consumer investment.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: Intuit
rows.basis: Normalized GAAP-like earnings including recurring SBC
rows.evidence: FY2026 revenue was $21.4B and GAAP EPS $16.46. FY2027 guidance is $23.28–23.51B revenue and $20.12–20.36 GAAP EPS. From FY2027, non-GAAP earnings include stock compensation.
rows.thesis: Small businesses need their books reconciled, payroll paid and taxes filed. Intuit already owns the records, distribution and expert escalation path. Better agents can increase task completion and service revenue; a free generic assistant still needs accurate records and execution.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $25.0B × 24% normalized net margin ÷ 267M diluted shares ≈ $22.50 EPS. This is above FY2027 GAAP guidance because calendar 2027 includes part of FY2028; it is not a restatement of company guidance.
rows.bearStory: Generic agents compress prices, small-business churn rises and live-service costs offset efficiency; $16 EPS at 14×.
rows.baseStory: QuickBooks, payments, payroll and assisted tax filing sustain growth; agent features improve retention and expert productivity.
rows.bullStory: Enterprise Suite and assisted services expand the customer wallet while agent productivity raises margins; $27 EPS at 30×.
catalysts: End-2026: FY2027 first-quarter growth and paid AI-service adoption.
Mid-2027: tax-season assisted-service economics, QuickBooks customer growth versus price increases, and churn.
End-2027: FY2028 outlook and evidence that agents expand revenue per business after support and inference costs.
rows.failure: Online ecosystem growth falls below 12% for two quarters, retention weakens, or tax/credit customer acquisition becomes structurally more expensive.
rows.risk: Tax policy, free filing, SMB failures, Mailchimp execution and credit-cycle exposure. A low multiple is insufficient if the customer relationship migrates elsewhere.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: GoDaddy
rows.basis: Normalized GAAP-like diluted earnings
rows.evidence: Q2 revenue grew 7%; Applications & Commerce grew 11%. Airo reached a $50M annualized bookings run rate. Management reaffirmed about $1.8B FY2026 FCF; June net debt was $2.7B.
rows.thesis: The distribution advantage is millions of existing entrepreneurs who need an online identity, a working site, bookings and payments. AI lowers setup effort and may improve attach rates. The outcome worth buying is a functioning business presence, not generated website code.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $5.67B × 21% normalized net margin ÷ 119M diluted shares ≈ $10 EPS. This needs high-single-digit revenue growth and continued net share reduction, not explosive domain growth.
rows.bearStory: AI-native builders and agent interfaces erode hosting and site-builder demand; $5.50 EPS at 11×.
rows.baseStory: Airo converts existing distribution into paid commerce features while the renewal base funds disciplined repurchases.
rows.bullStory: Agent identity and commerce APIs become meaningful paid products and higher-value attach grows; $12 EPS at 22×.
catalysts: End-2026: announced December 1 Investor Night; inspect paid Airo bookings and revised financial targets.
Mid-2027: renewal behavior of AI-acquired customers and Applications & Commerce growth.
End-2027: FCF per share after stock compensation, debt service and buybacks.
rows.failure: Airo usage fails to convert into paid renewals, or bookings growth stays below 3% while customer count declines.
rows.risk: The AI narrative is much smaller than the core business. Bookings run rate is not recognized recurring revenue; debt-financed repurchases can destroy value.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: Fabrinet
rows.basis: Normalized adjusted diluted EPS; SBC remains a valuation limitation
rows.evidence: Q4 FY2026 revenue was $1.316B, up 45%; GAAP EPS was $3.83 and adjusted EPS $4.10. FY2026 revenue rose 36% to about $4.6B.
rows.thesis: Qualified manufacturing, optical alignment, yield and reliable delivery can capture value across competing module architectures. Fabrinet offers exposure to optical volume without requiring one laser or DSP design to dominate.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $6.62B × 12.5% adjusted net margin ÷ 36M diluted shares ≈ $23 EPS. Revenue is about 26% above the Q4 run rate; the margin assumption requires continued mix and execution gains.
rows.bearStory: Customers digest inventory or move production in-house; $14 EPS at 17× reflects contract-manufacturing cyclicality.
rows.baseStory: Higher optical volumes and qualified capacity support growth while manufacturing execution preserves margins.
rows.bullStory: Multiple customers scale 1.6T and new production ramps faster; $29 EPS at 30×.
catalysts: End-2026: FY2027 guidance and order conversion into actual shipments.
Mid-2027: new capacity utilization, customer mix and 1.6T yields.
End-2027: sustained margin and cash conversion after growth investment.
rows.failure: Two quarters of sequential optical weakness, materially lower utilization, or loss of a major customer program.
rows.risk: Customer concentration, low switching volumes during qualification changes, Thailand operations and customer insourcing. Manufacturing revenue is not recurring software revenue.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: Reddit
rows.basis: Normalized diluted EPS; recurring SBC retained in model economics
rows.evidence: Q2 revenue was $805M, up 61%, with $762M advertising and $43M Other revenue. Diluted EPS was $1.25; fully diluted shares were about 207M.
rows.thesis: Human discussion and intent can improve ad relevance, search and licensed model data. The larger current earnings engine is advertising; treating all revenue as an AI-data royalty would misprice the business.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of $5.0B × 32% normalized net margin ÷ 200M diluted shares = $8 EPS. This needs substantial growth from the Q2 $3.22B annual run rate and stable economics; it is the most execution-sensitive consumer model.
rows.bearStory: AI answers reduce search referrals, commercial content harms engagement or advertisers slow; $3 EPS at 18×.
rows.baseStory: Ad tools monetize international users and intent better while human content remains valuable.
rows.bullStory: Ad relevance, international monetization and durable data access produce much higher earnings; $12 EPS at 42×.
catalysts: End-2026: ad revenue per user and logged-in engagement versus search-driven visits.
Mid-2027: international monetization and renewal terms on data agreements.
End-2027: per-share cash profitability after moderation, infrastructure and stock compensation.
rows.failure: Sustained engagement or referral declines accompanied by ad revenue growth below 20%, or dilution materially exceeds buybacks.
rows.risk: High traffic, platform, content-quality and regulatory risk. Its 1% portfolio weight is deliberately much smaller than its raw expected-value rank.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: Adobe
rows.basis: Normalized GAAP-like diluted earnings, retaining recurring SBC
rows.evidence: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $6.76B, up 13%; GAAP EPS was $4.62 versus $6.13 non-GAAP. Adobe reported AI-first ARR growth above 150% and $2.52B operating cash flow.
rows.thesis: Creation gets cheaper, but enterprises still need editing, permissions, brand consistency, approvals and document workflows. Adobe's opportunity is to monetize finished, governed output and creative iteration. The risk is real: lower-end creation may migrate to simpler products.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $29.46B × 28% normalized net margin ÷ 375M diluted shares ≈ $22 EPS. This is roughly 9% above the latest quarterly revenue run rate, with buybacks assisting per-share growth.
rows.bearStory: AI tools replace paid seats and credits fail to compensate; $14 EPS at 10× represents a structurally impaired franchise.
rows.baseStory: Professional workflows retain customers; AI credits and document products offset pricing pressure with moderate growth.
rows.bullStory: AI-generated content increases production volume and enterprise orchestration demand; $27 EPS at 24×.
catalysts: End-2026: FY2027 outlook, paid conversion and retention, rather than MAU growth alone.
Mid-2027: AI-credit gross profit and enterprise renewal economics.
End-2027: whether net new recurring revenue and cash profit per share grow together.
rows.failure: Creative recurring-revenue growth falls below 5%, net retention deteriorates, or inference costs rise without paid conversion.
rows.risk: Freemium usage is not monetization. Competition from Canva, model-native tools and platform bundling warrants the highest software bear probability in the model.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: Nvidia
rows.basis: Normalized diluted EPS; avoid investment gains; FY2027 non-GAAP includes SBC
rows.evidence: Q2 FY2027 revenue was $96.2B, data-center revenue $89.0B, and normalized non-GAAP EPS $2.22 versus GAAP $2.46. Q3 revenue guidance was $108B; Vera Rubin was already ramping.
rows.thesis: The advantage combines compute, software, networking and deployment speed. Agents can increase useful inference work, but token growth alone is insufficient: customers must earn enough to keep buying hardware.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $595B × 48% normalized net margin ÷ 23.8B diluted shares ≈ $12 EPS. This requires about 38% growth from the Q3 guided revenue run rate, rather than a repeat of recent triple-digit growth.
rows.bearStory: Capex digestion, custom accelerators and lower realized prices compress both profit and valuation; $6.50 EPS at 18×.
rows.baseStory: Rubin deployment and inference demand grow, with some margin normalization and buybacks.
rows.bullStory: Capacity converts into profitable agent and enterprise workloads with strong system economics; $16 EPS at 33×.
catalysts: End-2026: Rubin revenue conversion and customer cash-generation evidence.
Mid-2027: inference deployment economics, competitive accelerator adoption and supply execution.
End-2027: useful workload growth versus depreciation, financing obligations and next-platform transitions.
rows.failure: Sequential data-center revenue declines for two quarters with falling gross margin, or major customers cut orders while useful utilization deteriorates.
rows.risk: Customer concentration, export restrictions and financing feedback loops. The reported production ramp is already underway; a 2027 initial Rubin launch is not the catalyst.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: ServiceNow
rows.basis: Adjusted diluted EPS excluding SBC; use lower valuation and track dilution
rows.evidence: Q2 subscriptions rose 24.5% to $3.877B; cRPO grew 21%. ServiceNow AI exceeded $1B annual contract value. Management targeted SBC below 10% of revenue by 2029.
rows.thesis: Agents need workflow permissions, system connections, approval trails and accountability. ServiceNow can become the governance and execution layer across departments, provided paid AI activity expands the wallet faster than seat counts shrink.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $19.69B × 32% adjusted net margin ÷ 1.05B diluted shares ≈ $6 EPS. This is an adjusted-earnings model, not GAAP owner earnings; the SBC gap remains material.
rows.bearStory: Seat pressure and bundled platform agents impair growth; $3.50 adjusted EPS at 22×.
rows.baseStory: AI contracts convert into deployed workflows and renewals while existing enterprise distribution lowers selling costs.
rows.bullStory: Cross-department adoption and governance become standard budgets; $8 adjusted EPS at 45×.
catalysts: End-2026: cRPO quality, organic growth and AI ACV conversion.
Mid-2027: renewal cohorts, production deployments and sales efficiency.
End-2027: margin gains after cloud/inference expense and net dilution.
rows.failure: Organic cRPO growth below 15% for two quarters, or AI adoption rises while paid renewals and margins weaken.
rows.risk: ACV is not recognized revenue. Federal deal timing, acquisitions, Microsoft and Salesforce competition, and stock compensation can overstate the economics implied by adjusted EPS.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: Salesforce
rows.basis: Normalized adjusted diluted EPS excluding investment gains and SBC
rows.evidence: Q2 FY2027 revenue was $11.3B, including $456M from Informatica. Agentforce and Data 360 ARR approached $3.9B; Agentforce ARR exceeded $1.5B under an expanded definition.
rows.thesis: Sales, service and customer records are natural agent inputs, and enterprise distribution reduces go-to-market friction. The test is whether paid agent work adds profit after lost seats, model expense and acquisitions.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $51.4B × 28% normalized adjusted net margin ÷ 900M diluted shares ≈ $16 EPS. Repurchases help, but the model removes investment gains and does not annualize Q2's unusual EPS.
rows.bearStory: Seat erosion and acquisitions mask weak organic growth; $11 adjusted EPS at 14×.
rows.baseStory: Data integration and paid service-agent usage allow modest organic reacceleration.
rows.bullStory: Agent work expands the wallet and turns existing records into high-margin execution; $20 adjusted EPS at 28×.
catalysts: End-2026: organic cRPO and ARR definitions, acquisition integration and net buyback effect.
Mid-2027: paid usage, retention and service-cost savings.
End-2027: organic growth and profit after seat cannibalization establish a durable agent business.
rows.failure: Organic subscription growth remains below 5% despite fast reported AI ARR growth, or FCF per share fails to improve after buybacks.
rows.risk: Reported revenue includes acquired growth; agent ARR includes additional products. Neither a new name for existing revenue nor work-unit counts establish incremental demand.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: Toast
rows.basis: Normalized GAAP-like diluted EPS
rows.evidence: Q2 locations reached about 180k and ARR $2.4B. Recurring gross profit grew 31% on a GAAP basis; EPS was $0.26. Q2 FCF fell despite higher income.
rows.thesis: Restaurants buy labor savings, repeat visits and less administrative work. Toast already sees the transaction and operating context needed for useful agents. Its primary opportunity is merchant software and payments, not unproven sales of restaurant records to labs.
rows.bridge: CY2027 subscription-plus-fintech gross profit of about $2.95B × 32% net-income conversion ÷ 590M diluted shares ≈ $1.60 EPS. Gross-profit conversion is more useful here than a headline revenue multiple because payments include pass-through costs.
rows.bearStory: Restaurant closures, weak same-store demand and payments competition hurt growth; $0.80 EPS at 18×.
rows.baseStory: Location growth, useful paid AI features and operating leverage support earnings.
rows.bullStory: AI improves merchant sales and retention enough to expand attach and margins; $2.20 EPS at 38×.
catalysts: End-2026: IQ paid adoption, net new locations and gross profit per location.
Mid-2027: merchant retention and measurable labor or marketing ROI.
End-2027: cash conversion, profitability and expansion beyond the original restaurant base.
rows.failure: Location growth below 12% with declining recurring gross profit per location or rising merchant churn.
rows.risk: SMB credit and failure rates, consumer trade-down, processor competition and working-capital timing. AI usage must translate into merchant value and paid renewals.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: Broadcom
rows.basis: Normalized adjusted diluted EPS; cash generation and SBC checked separately
rows.evidence: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $29.6B and AI semiconductor revenue $16.7B. GAAP EPS was $2.68 versus $3.32 adjusted; quarterly FCF was $13.7B. Q4 AI revenue guidance was $21.7B.
rows.thesis: Custom accelerators and networking let hyperscalers optimize cost and power for predictable workloads. Broadcom can earn across accelerator silicon and the network, while infrastructure software supplies cash.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $189B × 45% adjusted net margin ÷ 5.0B diluted shares ≈ $17 EPS. This requires about 36% growth above the Q4 total-revenue guidance run rate and continued rich mix.
rows.bearStory: Large programs slip, customers concentrate design value internally and margins normalize; $10 adjusted EPS at 18×.
rows.baseStory: Custom programs ramp and Ethernet demand broadens, with software cash funding investment.
rows.bullStory: Multiple large accelerator programs scale alongside networking; $23 adjusted EPS at 34×.
catalysts: End-2026: Q4 AI revenue conversion and FY2027 program outlook.
Mid-2027: execution across more than one hyperscaler and networking attach.
End-2027: custom-silicon gross profit, customer concentration and repeat orders.
rows.failure: Program delays accompanied by declining AI revenue expectations or materially lower cash conversion.
rows.risk: A few buyers have enormous negotiating power. Revenue from custom systems can have different margins; AI revenue growth cannot be valued independently of incremental profit.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: RELX ADR
rows.basis: Adjusted EPS per NYSE ADR translated at assumed GBP/USD 1.30
rows.evidence: First-half revenue was £4.871B with 7% underlying growth; adjusted EPS was 68.6p and cash conversion 98%. Risk and Legal showed growth in embedded analytics and tools.
rows.thesis: Permissioned content, risk data and professional workflows are valuable when error costs matter. LexisNexis can sell ongoing decisions and task completion, not just text access. The US legal and insurance markets make this relevant to a US demand thesis.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of roughly £10.8B × 26.6% adjusted net margin ÷ 1.70B shares × assumed GBP/USD 1.30 ≈ $2.20 per ADR. FX is an explicit modeling assumption, not a quoted forward rate.
rows.bearStory: Professional agents bypass incumbent interfaces or procurement pressures pricing; $1.50 per ADR at 18×.
rows.baseStory: Paid legal and risk tools compound with modest margin expansion.
rows.bullStory: AI workflows improve product value and accelerate recurring growth; $2.60 per ADR at 30×.
catalysts: End-2026: underlying Legal and Risk growth, with attention to print-related comparison changes.
Mid-2027: renewal prices, AI attach and scientific-research customer retention.
End-2027: profit growth and cash conversion demonstrate that content access retains value.
rows.failure: Core Legal/Risk growth falls below 5% and customer retention weakens while AI development costs rise.
rows.risk: GBP translation, publishing and institutional budget pressure, and competition from Thomson Reuters and model-native legal tools. Watchlist weight reflects overlap with TRI and other data businesses.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: TSMC ADR
rows.basis: Normalized earnings per NYSE ADR in USD; five ordinary shares per ADR
rows.evidence: Q3 revenue was $46.72B and diluted EPS $4.60 per ADR. Gross margin was 66.4%; 2nm represented 8% of wafer revenue. Q4 revenue guidance was $52.3–54.3B.
rows.thesis: TSMC supplies competing GPU and custom-accelerator designers. That reduces the need to predict the winning chip architecture. Leading-edge manufacturing and packaging capacity remain difficult to replicate quickly.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $248B × 48% normalized net margin ÷ 5.18B ADR-equivalent diluted shares ≈ $23 EPS. This is roughly 16% above the Q4 guidance run rate; net margin is below Q3's 51.1%.
rows.bearStory: Demand digestion and overseas-fab costs compress profit; $14 per ADR at 17×. A Taiwan conflict could be much worse than this operating bear case.
rows.baseStory: 2nm, packaging and AI chip demand scale, with overseas costs partly offset by pricing and utilization.
rows.bullStory: Capacity expansion and leading-edge demand maintain exceptional returns; $29 per ADR at 30×.
catalysts: End-2026: 2nm ramp, Q4 guidance delivery and packaging utilization.
Mid-2027: 2nm/A16 execution and incremental capacity conversion; timing depends on customer qualifications.
End-2027: revenue per wafer, overseas margins and capital returns validate the capacity investment.
rows.failure: Leading-edge utilization deteriorates while capex stays high, or the technology/packaging execution advantage narrows materially.
rows.risk: Taiwan concentration is shared across much of the portfolio. Foreign listing status does not provide geographic operating diversification for US fabless chip holdings.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: Microsoft
rows.basis: Normalized diluted EPS excluding investment gains and unusual tax items
rows.evidence: FY2026 revenue was $331.8B. Azure surpassed $100B annual revenue and Microsoft 365 Copilot exceeded 30M paid seats. Q4 reported EPS contained investment and other discrete benefits.
rows.thesis: Existing enterprise procurement, identity and productivity workflows make Microsoft a natural agent distributor. Copilot, Azure and governance can monetize different parts of the stack; each must earn an adequate return on capital.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $396B × 43% normalized net margin ÷ 7.4B diluted shares ≈ $23 EPS. The scenario assumes growth plus operating leverage; it excludes mark-to-market investment gains.
rows.bearStory: AI spending outruns paid adoption and cloud depreciation rises; $18 EPS at 22×.
rows.baseStory: Azure capacity and paid productivity tools support durable growth despite ongoing investment.
rows.bullStory: Agent adoption becomes a broader productivity budget and margins hold; $27 EPS at 36×.
catalysts: End-2026: Azure growth versus capacity, Copilot paid adoption and capex guidance.
Mid-2027: enterprise renewal cohorts, utilization and cloud gross margin.
End-2027: cash returns after leases and capex establish whether AI revenue is economically attractive.
rows.failure: Copilot renewals disappoint while Azure growth and cloud margins both decelerate for two quarters.
rows.risk: Large contracted backlog is not immediate cash profit. Frontier-lab concentration, open-model pricing, regulatory scrutiny and rising depreciation matter.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: Credo
rows.basis: Normalized adjusted EPS with modeled dilution; large SBC gap remains
rows.evidence: Q1 FY2027 revenue was $479M, up 115% year over year. GAAP EPS was $0.67 versus $1.20 adjusted, and Q2 revenue guidance was $525–535M.
rows.thesis: Reliable short-reach copper links, optical DSPs and broader connectivity can coexist. The value proposition is delivered bandwidth, low power and fewer network interruptions; architecture changes create both new sockets and substitution risk.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $3.51B × 35% normalized adjusted net margin ÷ 205M diluted shares ≈ $6 EPS. This needs about 65% growth above the next-quarter revenue guidance run rate, making execution risk substantial.
rows.bearStory: Customer concentration, socket losses or optical substitution compress earnings; $2.50 adjusted EPS at 22×.
rows.baseStory: AEC demand persists while optical products expand the addressable mix.
rows.bullStory: Several major customers scale the portfolio across copper and optical links; $9 adjusted EPS at 50×.
catalysts: End-2026: revenue guidance conversion and customer diversification.
Mid-2027: 224G/1.6T shipments and acquired optical-platform integration.
End-2027: profitable new sockets, cash conversion and dilution-adjusted EPS.
rows.failure: A major design loss, sequential order weakness or persistent growth driven by a single buyer without diversification.
rows.risk: A 40× base multiple still assumes durable growth. The gap between GAAP and adjusted earnings is economically significant; a copper-versus-CPO binary is an inadequate thesis.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: SK hynix
rows.basis: Normalized K-IFRS-like EPS in KRW, excluding non-operating windfalls
rows.evidence: Q2 revenue was ₩79.3T and operating margin 76%. Net profit exceeded revenue, so it must not be annualized as operating earnings. HBM4 mass shipments began in Q2.
rows.thesis: HBM qualification, packaging and high-value memory mix create scarcity value, but conventional DRAM/NAND pricing still matters. Samsung's HBM4 progress is a direct competitive risk, not an automatic reason to assume perpetual shortages.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of about ₩400T × 36.5% normalized net margin ÷ 730M shares = ₩200k EPS. This deliberately normalizes profitability far below the latest quarter and strips non-operating windfalls.
rows.bearStory: Memory prices reverse, supply catches up and KRW weakens 10%; ₩60k EPS at 6×.
rows.baseStory: HBM and server mix retain above-cycle returns while conventional pricing moderates.
rows.bullStory: Scarcity and HBM execution persist; ₩300k EPS at 11× with 5% KRW appreciation.
catalysts: End-2026: HBM4 shipments, customer agreements and underlying operating cash flow.
Mid-2027: HBM4E qualification and yield, pricing and competitor supply.
End-2027: normalized profit and capex discipline after capacity additions.
rows.failure: HBM qualification/share losses plus falling conventional-memory prices, or contract visibility fails to convert into cash.
rows.risk: KRX access and KRW exposure are required. No OTC substitute or ADR liquidity is assumed. Zero allocation in the US implementation portfolio; US investors already hold overlapping memory exposure through MU.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: Verisk
rows.basis: Adjusted diluted EPS; cash conversion checked separately
rows.evidence: Q2 organic constant-currency revenue grew 5.8%, with 8% underlying subscription growth. Adjusted EPS was $1.98; FCF was $298M, benefiting partly from payment timing.
rows.thesis: Insurance decisions need standardized loss, repair, underwriting and claims data. AI can improve those decisions when embedded into existing processes. A model alone cannot cheaply reproduce validated industry data and acceptance.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $3.46B × 33% adjusted net margin ÷ 127M diluted shares ≈ $9 EPS. This requires high-single-digit revenue growth and moderate per-share leverage.
rows.bearStory: Insurers internalize workflows and pricing power weakens; $6.50 adjusted EPS at 20×.
rows.baseStory: Subscriptions and useful claims/underwriting tools compound with modest margin gains.
rows.bullStory: AI tools meaningfully expand customer spending; $10.50 EPS at 33×.
catalysts: End-2026: subscription growth and recovery toward management's operating targets.
Mid-2027: customer renewals and paid AI-workflow adoption.
End-2027: FCF growth after tax/vendor timing and acquisition effects.
rows.failure: Underlying subscription growth falls below 5% while retention or margins weaken.
rows.risk: Data regulation, insurer consolidation and slow industry procurement. This is a durable-data thesis with limited disclosed stand-alone generative-AI revenue; watchlist status avoids duplicating TRI/RELX exposure.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: Thomson Reuters
rows.basis: Adjusted diluted EPS; amortization and other exclusions require cash checks
rows.evidence: Q2 organic revenue grew 8%, with 10% growth in the Big 3 professional segments. Adjusted EPS was $0.99 and first-half adjusted EPS $2.22; Westlaw and CoCounsel contributed to growth.
rows.thesis: Professionals pay for trustworthy answers embedded in legal and tax work. Proprietary content, citations, workflow integration and institutional procurement provide a stronger monetization path than undifferentiated data resale.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $9.2B × 26.2% adjusted net margin ÷ 430M diluted shares ≈ $5.60 EPS. Growth and margin expansion must both contribute; the model does not annualize a seasonally weak quarter.
rows.bearStory: Legal AI competitors compress pricing and professional seat counts; $4 adjusted EPS at 15×.
rows.baseStory: CoCounsel attaches to the existing base while content and workflow improve retention and pricing.
rows.bullStory: Agent workflows materially expand professional spending and margins; $7 EPS at 30×.
catalysts: End-2026: recurring organic growth and CoCounsel monetization.
Mid-2027: tax-season contribution, legal renewals and incremental AI gross profit.
End-2027: content-powered agents support pricing and earnings after implementation costs.
rows.failure: Big 3 organic growth falls below 6% while AI spending and development costs rise.
rows.risk: The investment depends on trusted workflow economics, not merely owning text. Harvey and other private entrants can own the interface; model vendors can bundle research.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: Micron
rows.basis: Normalized GAAP-like diluted EPS; cycle-adjusted rather than peak annualization
rows.evidence: Q4 FY2026 revenue was $54.23B and GAAP EPS $32.87, with 86.8% gross margin. Q1 FY2027 GAAP EPS guidance was $37.84 ± $1.00.
rows.thesis: Agent workloads need HBM, server memory and persistent storage, but the stock's outcome depends on price discipline and normalized profitability. A low P/E measured against scarcity earnings can be a trap.
rows.bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $253B × 50% normalized net margin ÷ 1.15B diluted shares ≈ $110 EPS. The model is below annualized Q1 guided EPS of about $151; even the base assumes unusually high memory margins.
rows.bearStory: ASP compression and capacity growth overwhelm bit demand; $40 EPS at 7× produces a severe drawdown.
rows.baseStory: HBM/server mix and contracts preserve elevated returns while margins normalize.
rows.bullStory: Scarcity lasts and capacity execution is strong; $165 EPS at 14×. This case needs pricing and cash collection, not only shipment growth.
catalysts: End-2026: contracted pricing, HBM allocation and Q1 guidance delivery.
Mid-2027: HBM4E production, competitor yields and DRAM/NAND price trends.
End-2027: through-cycle FCF after capex, inventories and customer receivables.
rows.failure: Two sequential price/margin deteriorations with rising inventories or receivables, especially if capex remains aggressive.
rows.risk: 35% operating bear probability and only 2% allocation reflect cycle exposure. The report does not infer future returns from the previous memory rally.
rows.classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

rows.name: Meta Platforms
rows.basis: Normalized diluted EPS; exclude exceptional legal/severance and tax distortions
rows.evidence: Q2 revenue grew 28%, with ad impressions up 14% and price per ad up 12%. Operating income fell 8%; FCF was only $784M as capex reached $31.1B.

rows.name: Uber
rows.basis: Normalized non-GAAP; remove investment revaluations and unusual tax items
rows.evidence: Q2 gross bookings were $58.0B, trips grew 18%, normalized EPS was $0.81 and trailing free cash flow exceeded $10B. GAAP EPS of $1.17 included investment gains.
rows.thesis: The scarce asset is aggregated demand, payments, dispatch and local supply. AI can improve matching and support before autonomy is economically material. The strongest version of the thesis is that autonomous fleets need distribution; it is not that Uber must win vehicle manufacturing.
rows.bridge: CY2027 gross bookings of about $285B × 3.2% normalized net-income conversion ÷ 2.03B diluted shares ≈ $4.50 EPS. This requires roughly 23% growth over the Q2 bookings run rate and a modest conversion improvement.
rows.bearStory: Autonomous operators retain customers, insurance and driver costs rise, and delivery competition forces incentives; $2.60 EPS and a 16× multiple.
rows.baseStory: Demand and cross-platform usage grow; dispatch, advertising and operating efficiency improve earnings without requiring a mass robotaxi rollout.
rows.bullStory: Autonomous partnerships expand supply while Uber retains distribution economics; $5.60 EPS and 34× require strong booking growth and confidence in durable take rates.
catalysts: End-2026: Q3/Q4 booking growth, EPS conversion and autonomous-partner unit economics.
Mid-2027: evidence that autonomous markets add incremental profitable trips rather than subsidized volume.
End-2027: repeat usage, buybacks and normalized earnings establish whether the marketplace remains the customer interface.
rows.failure: Two quarters of bookings growth below 12% with deteriorating normalized operating margin, or demonstrable loss of customer ownership to autonomous fleets.
rows.risk: High disruption uncertainty. Premium rides are only one use case; this is not a pure luxury-consumer investment.

End-2027: whether net new recurring revenue and cash profit per share grow together.
rows.failure: Creative recurring-revenue growth falls below 5%, net retention deteriorates, or inference costs rise without paid conversion.
rows.risk: Freemium usage is not monetization. Competition from Canva, model-native tools and platform bundling warrants the highest software bear probability in the model.

rows.basis: Normalized diluted EPS; avoid investment gains; FY2027 non-GAAP includes SBC

rows.baseStory: Rubin deployment and inference demand grow, with some margin normalization and buybacks.

End-2027: useful workload growth versus depreciation, financing obligations and next-platform transitions.
rows.failure: Sequential data-center revenue declines for two quarters with falling gross margin, or major customers cut orders while useful utilization deteriorates.
rows.risk: Customer concentration, export restrictions and financing feedback loops. The reported production ramp is already underway; a 2027 initial Rubin launch is not the catalyst.

rows.risk: SMB credit and failure rates, consumer trade-down, processor competition and working-capital timing. AI usage must translate into merchant value and paid renewals.

## What is being ranked

Prepared **October 22, 2026**, using **October 16 regular-session closing prices** as the common entry point. The horizon is December 31, 2027, approximately 14½ months. These are October 2026 historical prices, not live execution quotes. US-listed instruments are in USD; SK hynix is its KRX ordinary share in KRW.

I interpret the later US scope as **US economic demand and practical US-investor implementation**, while allowing globally headquartered suppliers and data franchises. The ranking includes UK, Canadian, Taiwanese, Korean and US businesses. SK hynix requires Korean-market access and receives no allocation in the US implementation portfolio.

“Highest expected value” cannot be established objectively across every listed company. This is a **judgmental top 25 among the researched candidates**, selected for an identifiable AI-to-profit path, sufficient disclosed economics, plausible 2027 proof points and an investable valuation. It is not an exhaustive global stock screen or a claim that an unmodeled small cap cannot outperform. Japanese and mainland Chinese suppliers remain a coverage limitation.

All stock scenarios are **my estimates**. Filings and earnings releases establish the operating starting point, not the price targets or probabilities. The selected company releases predate the entry date; current undated data-licensing pages are used as present-day business-model evidence. This is research prepared today around a fixed entry reference, not a reconstructed historical backtest.

Use the ranking to prioritize diligence, the company analyses to challenge assumptions, and the portfolio weights to manage shared risks. No trade execution is part of this report.

rows.section: The K-shaped economy is useful, but it is not a single trade
rows.classification: Source-backed qualitative analysis; inference identified in text
rows.analysis:
## The K-shaped economy is useful, but it is not a single trade

**Separate wealth, income growth, affordability and spending behavior.** Asset owners can gain wealth while wage growth converges; a household can feel poorer despite increasing nominal spending. Age, income, homeownership, geography, debt and family formation are different dimensions.

The most relevant current evidence is mixed:

| Claim | What the evidence supports | Investment implication |
|---|---|---|
| Inflation is still a constraint | September CPI rose 3.7% year over year and 0.6% month over month; gasoline rose 9.1% in the month. | Do not assume rapid rate cuts or automatic valuation expansion. |
| Lower-income consumption is collapsing | Bank of America reported September nominal card-spending growth of 6.2%, or 5.1% excluding gasoline, and broader growth across income cohorts. Its August report still identified unusually strong top-5% spending. | A wealth divide can coexist with improving lower-income spending growth. |
| Credit stress is spreading uncontrollably | New York Fed Q2 debt was $18.8T; 4.7% was delinquent. Credit-card serious-delinquency transitions were elevated but roughly steady. | Monitor deterioration; do not infer an imminent aggregate consumption crash from high debt balances alone. |
| Housing is a buyer’s market | Redfin estimated 62.6% more sellers than buyers in September, with 41 of 50 large metros classified as buyer’s markets. | Transaction frictions, repair/remodel activity and local price concessions can persist. |
| All sub-$1M homes are crashing; all $5M+ homes are booming | The sources do not establish those nationwide price cutoffs. Redfin’s luxury definition and metro mix differ. | Require local inventory, completed transactions and price-tier data before making a housing trade. |
| Travel and Airbnb are collapsing | Airbnb reported Q2 revenue growth of 17% and Nights and Seats Booked growth of 10%. Delta reported broad September demand strength. | Weak individual hosts or mass-market travel cohorts do not establish platform-wide collapse. |

Sources: [BLS September CPI](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/cpi_10142026.htm), [October consumer spending](https://institute.bankofamerica.com/economic-insights/consumer-checkpoint-october-2026.html), [August income-cohort discussion](https://institute.bankofamerica.com/economic-insights/consumer-checkpoint-august-2026.html), [New York Fed household credit](https://www.newyorkfed.org/newsevents/news/research/2026/20260811/), [Redfin housing balance](https://www.redfin.com/news/buyers-vs-sellers-september-2026/), [Airbnb Q2](https://news.airbnb.com/airbnb-q2-2026-financial-results), [Delta Q3](https://ir.delta.com/news/news-details/2026/Delta-Air-Lines-Announces-September-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx).

The Fed raised its target range to **3.75%–4.00% in September**, explicitly citing elevated inflation. That supports a financing constraint, not certainty that rates must remain unchanged through 2027. [September FOMC statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm).

### How human behavior changes the opportunity

Small affordable treats can satisfy convenience, reward and social participation when larger aspirations feel unattainable. That is a plausible hypothesis for some consumers, not verified proof that people order delivery because they have abandoned homeownership. Time scarcity, dual-income schedules, disability, promotions and subscription economics can produce the same behavior.

The investable distinction is **frequency × contribution profit × retention**. More orders driven by subsidies can destroy shareholder value. A $30 delivery order is not equivalent to $30 of platform revenue, and platform revenue is not equivalent to free cash flow.

At the wealthy end, customers buy time, access, certainty and status. AI can make discovery and coordination cheaper; scarce restaurant tables, trusted human service and desirable locations can retain pricing power. An $80 matcha or a private-club waitlist is evidence of a niche willingness to pay, not an estimate of market size.

A useful segmentation for this portfolio is:

- **Financially constrained:** lower prices, essential goods, lower administrative costs and value-for-money services. AI beneficiaries include SMB tools that save real labor; merchant failure rates remain the counterweight.
- **Stable earners with limited time:** trusted automation, accounting, payments, travel and convenience. Distribution and integration matter more than model novelty.
- **Affluent asset owners:** premium experiences, privacy, access and concierge service. The wealth effect helps demand, but a stock-market downturn can reverse both spending and advertising.
- **Businesses facing labor and financing pressure:** tools that recover revenue, reduce errors or complete tasks with little implementation effort. This is the strongest cross-income AI adoption mechanism.

These are economic hypotheses to test against cohorts and unit economics, not demographic stereotypes.

rows.section: Follow the path from a useful task to retained profit
rows.classification: Source-backed qualitative analysis; inference identified in text
rows.analysis:
## Follow the path from a useful task to retained profit

A useful AI demonstration becomes investable when someone has a budget, the system can act reliably, the customer keeps paying, and the provider retains profit after inference, support, distribution and capital costs.

The practical sequence is:

1. **A costly task exists.** Missed restaurant bookings, unreconciled accounts, slow insurance estimates, customer-service queues or underused compute.
2. **The provider has context and permission to act.** Records, payment credentials, workflow integrations, audit trails and an escalation path.
3. **Adoption is easy enough.** Existing distribution, a familiar invoice and measurable ROI can beat a technically superior product requiring a new implementation.
4. **The payment model captures the value.** A seat, transaction, completed task or premium subscription must produce incremental gross profit.
5. **Competition and capital spending leave a return for shareholders.** Falling model costs can help customers while competition gives away the savings.

| Layer | What the customer pays for | Public candidates | What must be proven |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compute and fabrication | Useful deployed capacity | NVDA, TSM, AVGO | Utilization, customer returns, cash collection |
| Memory and connectivity | Bandwidth, reliability, working capacity | MU, SK hynix, FN, COHR, CRDO | Yield, qualification, pricing and supply discipline |
| Power and cooling | Operational racks delivered on time | VRT, ETN | Accepted projects and cash-generating backlog |
| Enterprise workflows | Work completed with controls | MSFT, NOW, CRM, INTU, ADBE | Paid renewals after inference and lost seats |
| Trusted professional data | Decisions that can be defended | TRI, RELX, VRSK | Incremental paid usage and retained authority |
| SMB go-to-market | More customers and less administration | GDDY, TOST | Paid conversion, lower churn and merchant ROI |
| Consumer distribution and advertising | Matching demand to supply | UBER, META, GOOGL, AMZN, RDDT | Incremental contribution profit and retention |

These exposures overlap. Microsoft can benefit from agent adoption while paying Nvidia, and those revenues are not independent sources of portfolio diversification.

**My strongest general thesis is that cheaper intelligence raises the value of distribution, trusted context and execution.** It can also reduce the price of software features and generic data. Owning records is useful only when the business has the right to use them and can convert that advantage into a paid product.

rows.section: The physical bottleneck changes as architectures and supply change
rows.classification: Source-backed qualitative analysis; inference identified in text
rows.analysis:
## The physical bottleneck changes as architectures and supply change

Memory and storage were logical beneficiaries of rising AI workloads. They were not guaranteed “easy money”: at each entry price the investor still had to forecast supply, qualification, pricing, financing and what the market already expected. A correct industry forecast can produce a poor stock return if profits normalize or the entry multiple is too high.

### Memory: distinguish structural demand from a pricing cycle

Training and inference need different mixes of HBM, conventional DRAM, server low-power memory and storage. Longer-running agents can expand working context and persistent state. But better caching, quantization, compression, routing and memory sharing can reduce hardware required per task. Lower cost can stimulate usage; the net effect on supplier revenue is an empirical question.

Micron’s unusually high reported margins make **normalized earnings** decisive. The model’s $110 base EPS is below annualized near-term guidance, yet still assumes extraordinary industry profitability. SK hynix’s reported net profit exceeded revenue in Q2; operating earnings and cash collection are more useful anchors than headline net income. [Micron Q4](https://investors.micron.com/news/press-release/2026/Micron-Technology-Inc--Reports-Record-Fiscal-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2026-Results/), [SK hynix Q2](https://news.skhynix.com/en/q2-2026-business-results/).

Samsung’s current HBM4 and HBM4E progress means competition cannot be omitted from a scarcity thesis. Watch qualification, yield and conventional-memory supply alongside customer agreements. Agreements improve visibility, but their pricing, volume flexibility and credit terms determine protection. [Samsung Q2 results](https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-second-quarter-2026-results).

### Optics: CPO is a change in value capture, not a universal buy signal

CPO places optical engines near switching or compute silicon. It can reduce electrical distance and power, but adds packaging, thermal, test, serviceability and production challenges. Pluggable modules, near-packaged optics, external lasers and short-reach copper can coexist across distances and architectures.

Nvidia already described Spectrum-6 systems supporting **both pluggable and co-packaged optics** in its August release. Lumentum announced an external-laser module with initial availability expected in **1H2027**. Those are concrete product references; neither establishes that all network connections become CPO by 2027. [Nvidia earnings](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-second-quarter-fiscal-2027), [Lumentum product announcement](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-to-Demonstrate-DWDM-ELSFP-Laser-Module-for-OCI-MSA-Applications-at-ECOC-2026/default.aspx).

The relevant competitive questions differ:

- **Fabrinet:** can qualified manufacturing scale across customer designs, and does volume growth retain attractive margins?
- **Coherent/Lumentum:** who owns qualified laser and optical-component capacity, and how much system value remains with them?
- **Credo/Astera:** which electrical, DSP, retimer and rack-connectivity sockets survive or expand as distances and architectures change?
- **Arista/Broadcom/Nvidia:** who controls switching silicon, systems, software and the customer relationship?
- **AOI and other module makers:** can announced capacity become qualified, profitable shipments before supply catches up?

Optical demand growth can coincide with falling average selling prices. In-source designs can move profit toward hyperscalers or silicon vendors. The portfolio therefore owns several distinct capabilities but limits their combined size.

### Power and deployment may monetize before new model features

A rack awaiting power or commissioning produces no useful tokens. Eaton and Vertiv address deliverability and operation, not simply model performance. Their demand can be more architecture-agnostic, but it is still exposed to customer capex, permitting, grid constraints and project financing.

The next bottleneck could be deployment labor, testing, power electronics, data access or customer integration. I would buy an identified order-to-profit mechanism, not rotate automatically from the last winner into the nearest adjacent component.

rows.section: The data-broker opportunity is real; recurring economics are the harder part
rows.classification: Source-backed qualitative analysis; inference identified in text
rows.analysis:
## The data-broker opportunity is real; recurring economics are the harder part

Mercor publicly offers to license company workflow data, process it and pay the business. Its stated inputs include communications, code and business-system records, and its payout depends on volume and depth. That verifies the existence of a market-facing business model. It does **not** independently verify buyer budgets, broker profits, typical seller payouts, or the claim that visiting small restaurants and salons routinely generates millions per month. [Mercor Data](https://www.mercor.com/data/).

The unverified viral claim combines several different businesses:

| Business | Potential source of value | Main economic weakness |
|---|---|---|
| One-time archive licensing | Scarce records of real work | Finite inventory; nonrecurring revenue |
| Data brokerage/referrals | Finding sellers and arranging access | Buyer concentration; low switching costs |
| Cleaning and labeling | Quality, de-identification and expert evaluation | Labor cost, procurement pressure, automation |
| Agent environments and evaluation | Realistic tasks and measurable outcomes | Expensive maintenance; specialized expertise |
| Live workflow software | Ongoing context, permissions and execution | Integration costs and incumbent competition |
| Professional decision products | Trusted data plus domain-specific output | Interface disintermediation and liability |

A useful private-company diligence checklist is therefore commercial: named and repeat buyers, recognized revenue versus bookings, gross margin after expert labor, repeat-license rights, concentration, retention, collections, and the cost of replacing a sold dataset. Payment for one large archive is not monthly recurring revenue.

Data access also has contractual and privacy constraints. De-identification is one processing step; the investment still depends on usable rights, permitted purposes and enforceable customer relationships. The report assumes no unauthorized resale of merchant, employee or patient records.

For public equities, **TRI, RELX and VRSK** offer existing professional-data economics. **INTU, TOST and CRM** offer useful workflow context and distribution, without any assumption that they sell customer records to labs. **RDDT** has a direct data-access angle, but its reported advertising business is much larger than Other revenue. These are distinct mechanisms, not interchangeable “data plays.”

Private companies such as Mercor, Scale AI, Surge AI, Handshake, Harvey and vertical-agent startups are competitive context, not securities available in this public-equity portfolio. No current private valuation or ownership status is assumed here. A small private operator can have exceptional economics that are immaterial inside a large public parent; proxy exposure must be checked for size and terms.

rows.section: Luxury and small treats matter through distribution and unit economics
rows.classification: Source-backed qualitative analysis; inference identified in text
rows.analysis:
## Luxury and small treats matter through distribution and unit economics

Your consumer observations are useful leads. To turn them into a stock thesis, identify which company owns supply, the customer relationship, the payment and the repeat purchase.

**Premium access and concierge.** The value is often a scarce reservation, a trusted operator or a human who solves a difficult problem. AI can lower the cost of searching, planning and coordination, while making generic concierge chat easier to copy. Public candidates for a separate affluent-spending portfolio include American Express, Booking Holdings, premium hotel managers, luxury brands and selected travel operators. Their returns require card, occupancy, fee, credit and valuation analysis; the AI angle alone does not earn them a top-25 place here.

American Express’s investor materials identify its premium-lifestyle positioning and a proposed TheFork acquisition. That supports a distribution/access strategy, not a conclusion that every reservation is oversubscribed or that AI is its primary profit driver. [American Express investor releases](https://ir.americanexpress.com/news/investor-relations-news/default.aspx).

Aman, Blacklane, private clubs and an “Atlas” concierge-card anecdote should not be mapped to a ticker without verifying the exact entity, ownership and economics. This report does not treat them as stand-alone public equities or assume public shareholders own material exposure to them.

**Convenience and affordable rewards.** Uber and Toast can benefit from habitual demand and better merchant operations. The useful AI link is improved matching, marketing, support and order economics. There is no verified causal evidence here that abandoning homeownership is the main reason for delivery spending. DoorDash is a relevant competitor and candidate, but the thesis must survive fulfillment costs, merchant fees, promotions and valuation.

**Value-oriented consumption.** Walmart, Costco, TJX, Ross and other value retailers can benefit from trade-down or convenience. AI may improve inventory, labor planning and retail advertising. This is a separate margin/distribution thesis; a defensive business can still have an unattractive stock price. Dollar stores are not automatic winners when their customers are under pressure.

**Healthcare, insurance and essential services.** Documentation, scheduling, coding, claims and collections can create measurable AI savings. The constraint is trusted integration and accountability, not a lack of possible use cases. Verisk supplies one mature public route. Healthcare-service companies need reimbursement, utilization and liability analysis before AI efficiency can be credited to shareholders.

These broader areas inform the opportunity map, but have not all received a full three-scenario valuation. They are **candidates for comparison**, not rejected stocks proven to have lower expected returns.

## The 2027 catalysts are proof points, not just product launch dates

The company analyses distinguish announced events from **analyst underwriting milestones**. A reporting season is an opportunity for evidence, not a promised share-price catalyst.

| Window | What is likely to change the investment case | Evidence to demand |
|---|---|---|
| End-2026 | Guidance for 2027, infrastructure order conversion, paid AI renewals and capital budgets | Organic growth, committed versus recognized revenue, cash collection, cost to serve |
| 1H2027 | Tax-season economics; enterprise renewal cohorts; 1.6T/HBM/customer qualifications; electrical transaction milestones | Net retention, paid tasks, yields, utilization, accepted shipments, gross profit |
| 2H2027 / year-end | Whether the first large deployment cohorts produce durable profit | FCF after capex and leases, dilution-adjusted EPS, renewal behavior, pricing and supply discipline |

Concrete references include **GoDaddy’s December 1, 2026 Investor Night**, **Vertiv’s October 28, 2026 earnings**, **Lumentum’s expected 1H2027 external-laser availability**, and **Eaton’s expected Q1 2027 Mobility separation**. The latter two remain management expectations, not guaranteed dates. [GoDaddy filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1609711/000160971126000087/gddyex991-20260630xq2earni.htm), [Vertiv date](https://investors.vertiv.com/news/news-details/2026/Vertiv-Announces-Date-of-Third-Quarter-2026-Earnings-Release-and-Conference-Call/), [Lumentum release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-to-Demonstrate-DWDM-ELSFP-Laser-Module-for-OCI-MSA-Applications-at-ECOC-2026/default.aspx), [Eaton results](https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-reports-record-second-quarter-2026-results.html).

**My priorities by window:** End-2026 favors earnings and guidance checks in INTU, GDDY, NVDA, AVGO and FN. By mid-2027, INTU's tax season, NOW/CRM renewals and FN/COHR/CRDO qualifications should provide more operating evidence. By end-2027, the deciding measure across MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META and the agent vendors is cash profit after the infrastructure and service bill. Memory stays conditional on pricing and cash collection throughout; a calendar date alone does not justify increasing it.

For agents, the important inflection is **pilot → paid deployment → repeat use → renewal → profit**. Revenue can lag bookings, and profit can lag revenue. For hardware, it is **design win → qualification → volume shipment → acceptance → cash**. Market prices can anticipate each stage well before the income statement.

An agent that reduces labor cost is not automatically additive for its software vendor. Fewer seats, outcome-based pricing and competition can transfer the savings to the customer. Likewise, a component supplier can ship more bits or ports and earn less if pricing normalizes.

They are not fully valued here. China's optical suppliers and Japan's materials/test companies deserve direct local-market research; excluding unverified prices is preferable to inventing global coverage.

For private companies, use them to test competition and customer demand. Do not capitalize a startup's headline revenue into a public proxy without checking ownership, preferred terms, dilution and materiality.

rows.section: What would make me change the portfolio
rows.classification: Source-backed qualitative analysis; inference identified in text
rows.analysis:
## What would make me change the portfolio

Review the same small set of evidence each quarter. These are decision rules, not an automated trading instruction.

| Test | Evidence strengthening the thesis | Evidence weakening it |
|---|---|---|
| End-customer AI ROI | Paid renewals, lower cost per completed task, higher useful utilization | Rising usage with weak conversion or persistent subsidies |
| Hardware demand quality | Accepted shipments, collections, stable inventory and customer returns | Receivables/inventory outrun sales; orders shift without cash |
| Memory/optical pricing | Qualified supply and mix support profit despite more volume | ASP and margins fall faster than bit/port demand grows |
| Software value capture | AI wallet expansion exceeds lost seats and inference cost | Rebranded ARR, acquired growth or activity counts mask weak organic revenue |
| Consumer behavior | Cohort retention and contribution profit improve | Promotions drive transactions while profitability deteriorates |
| Financing | Capex funded by durable customer cash generation | Vendor/customer financing and equity issuance sustain uneconomic demand |
| K-shaped macro | Affordability stabilizes without a collapse in asset wealth | Credit deterioration, unemployment and wealth declines reinforce one another |

**Increase conviction** when revenue, gross profit and cash tell the same story. **Reduce conviction** when management changes metric definitions, highlights total activity without paid economics, or needs increasingly generous financing to maintain growth.

The largest unresolved questions are the durability of scarcity margins, who owns the agent interface, and how much incremental AI profit is left after capex and stock compensation. Those questions determine whether the model’s base cases are conservative or optimistic.

The ranking is most useful as a set of falsifiable investment theses. It should be updated when prices, filings or customer economics change; it should not be defended simply because the AI story remains exciting.

evidenceFlow.title: Observed versus modeled
evidenceFlow.detail: Reference prices and stated historical financial metrics are observed source inputs. All 2027 earnings, terminal multiples, probabilities, FX moves, portfolio weights and expected returns are analyst scenarios; they are not reported company guidance.

evidenceFlow.title: Reproduce calculations
evidenceFlow.detail: For each company: bear=bearEPS*bearPE; base=baseEPS*basePE; bull=bullEPS*bullPE. evPrice=(bear*bearProbability*bearFX+base*baseProbability*baseFX+bull*bullProbability*bullFX)/100. expectedReturn=evPrice/price-1. downside=bear*bearFX/price-1. dollars=weight*1000. buyCeiling=evPrice/1.25. Rank descending expectedReturn. Price is the regular-session close on 2026-10-16; no dividend adjustment is used. All target EPS, multiples, probabilities, FX assumptions and diluted-share bridges are analyst assumptions. No YTD returns enter the calculation.

metricDefinitions.label: Expected price return
metricDefinitions.definition: Probability-weighted end-2027 price divided by October 16, 2026 regular-session close, minus one. No dividends, taxes, fees or cash interest. KRW scenario translation applies only to SK hynix.

metricDefinitions.label: End-2027 price
metricDefinitions.definition: Calendar-2027 normalized diluted EPS times an analyst-selected year-end 2027 P/E; instrument currency is stated per company.

metricDefinitions.label: Bear downside
metricDefinitions.definition: Operating bear terminal price, adjusted for modeled currency movement, divided by reference price minus one. This is not a maximum-loss estimate.

metricDefinitions.label: Entry ceiling
metricDefinitions.definition: Expected terminal price divided by 1.25, preserving a 25% modeled cumulative price return. This is not intrinsic value or a guarantee.

metricDefinitions.label: Portfolio allocation
metricDefinitions.definition: Weight is percent of the full $100,000 target portfolio. Dollar budget equals weight times $1,000. The residual 8% is cash; displayed stress values assume full target allocation at reference prices.

methods.code: dollars=100000*weight/100; contribution=weight/100*expectedReturn; cash=100000-sum(stock dollars). Terminal portfolio values sum dollars*(scenario price/reference price), plus cash.

rows.scenario: Expected: shift 10 points bull to bear

source.label: Deterministic scenario aggregation; no estimated joint probabilities
source.notes: Synchronized endpoints are stress illustrations, not probabilistic portfolio forecasts. Company probabilities differ and no covariance model was estimated.

evidenceFlow.title: Aggregate terminal values
evidenceFlow.detail: Sum each target dollar holding times the respective scenario price/reference-price ratio, plus $8,000 cash. Use KRW translation multipliers for SK hynix; its weight is zero.

evidenceFlow.title: Probability sensitivity
evidenceFlow.detail: For each equity holding shift 0.10 probability from its bull endpoint to bear. Delta=value*(bear*bearFX-bull*bullFX)/price*0.10. Leave base unchanged.

metricDefinitions.label: Terminal portfolio value
metricDefinitions.definition: Deterministic weighted value of target allocations. Returns exclude income, taxes and costs.
